correctness.rationale: The rational dispersion has one root in each exterior real interval. The interior minimum yields the exact threshold and one complex-conjugate pair; its growth vanishes at both ends. Implicit differentiation forces one of two possible upper-half-plane rays for the complex fractional separation. The positive ray gives a strictly increasing unique ratio parametrization; the other ray gives strictly negative implied squared wavenumber and is impossible. The actual unique global maximum and its frequency follow by substitution. At fixed P, the identity (r^4+2r^3+2r+1)-6r^2=(r-1)^2(r^2+4r+1) yields a sharp bound. The included standalone checker passed six symbolic identities and 7,254 numerical assertions.

value.rationale: The ratio-free one-dimensional cold two-stream problem is a natural benchmark for beam-plasma temporal instability. The theorem solves the global parameterized peak-growth design across every positive density imbalance, proves its unique optimizing wavelength and a sharp physically interpretable balance law at constant total plasma-frequency weight. These combine a nontrivial stationary-point exclusion and exact inequality; not merely a textbook equal-density exercise.
